rationale.complete: Round 1 done: card and dated predictions before data; synthetic validation on 15 real skeletons (11,600 replicates, registered and added worlds) committed with Amendment A1 before real data; replication on 15 testable units in 8 regime-III periods x 3 vector variants x 3 drive modes; NE41 native; 475 estimates rows. Missing: no confirm script (nothing resolved to confirm); gamma_kick not re-estimated in shared weeks.
rationale.faithfulness: The model's unfitted prediction is 7 to >1,000x below resolution in every unit, so the HH382 test is untestable (inconclusive). The slow part behaves (gamma_s ~0.013/call in #51, R_slow 1.06 across erasures), but the fast form is contradicted at lag 1 (dip in 14/15 units, post hoc). Scorecard A1 B1 C0 D0 E1 F1 G0 H0 I0.
rationale.usefulness: A negative result about method: the read channel cannot be seen in total content variance at village data sizes; measure it along sender directions instead.

one_line: The read-driven fast content variance predicted from H130's kick (median 0.0044, ~2.5% of dynamic variance) is 7 to >1,000x below what the own autocovariance resolves in 15 regime-III units: HH382's variance split is untestable (inconclusive, below resolution).

models.note: Two-rate form: fast amplitude below resolution in every unit; slow rate ~0.013/call in #51
Linear vector dynamics on the call clock; read-kick share of variance unresolvable

v2.claim: In 15 regime-III units the read-driven fast content variance predicted from H130's kick (median A_k^pred 0.0044, about 2.5% of the dynamic variance) lies 7 to more than 1,000 times below the smallest resolvable fast amplitude, so HH382's variance-split test is untestable at this data size
